content.text:
You are a veteran Capcom NES pixel artist and animator for Mega Man 2-3. You are shown the 2 frames of ONE
looping enemy animation, left to right, at 1x (true size, left) and enlarged with nearest-neighbour scaling (right),
on a neutral grey-blue background that is not part of the sprite. The animation loops: after the last frame comes
the first again.

Below the frames is a DIFFERENCE row, computed exactly from the pixels: one panel per loop step (frame 1 -> 2,
2 -> 3, ..., last -> 1). Pixels that change in that step are MAGENTA; unchanged pixels are dimmed grey. Use it to
see the motion precisely: if a panel has no magenta, nothing moves in that step. Do not claim changes the
difference row does not show.

Below that is a TIMELINE row: the loop sampled every 4 game frames (1/15 s) at 60 fps, so each frame repeats in
proportion to how long it is held. Timing: frame 1: 28 game frames (467 ms), frame 2: 10 game frames (167 ms); loop 38 game frames (633 ms).

The enemy: "A small floating robot squid, Blooper-like, that swims along at and after Mega Man in pulses (tentacles gather, then thrust). It is a swimming mine: when it gets close its eyes flash red, then it explodes."
The intended motion: "swim in pulses: frame 1 (the approved still) is the glide, tentacles together; frame 2 is the stroke, tentacles flared out wide as it pushes; looping"
Its behaviour in the game: "moves toward Mega Man in pulses about every 40 game frames: a short gather (tentacles flare, a brief tell), then a quick stroke that shoots it forward and a long glide that slows down with the tentacles together"
Game: Mega Man 2-3 (NES).

Judge whether this is a convincing authentic NES Mega Man enemy animation showing the intended motion. Be
calibrated: authentic Capcom enemy animations score about 90-95; competent fan work about 60-70; amateur or
AI-looking work about 30-45. Do not reward or punish an animation for being recognisable; judge what you see.

Criteria, 0-10 each:
- motion_readability: the intended motion reads clearly when the frames loop
- consistency: the same character in every frame (same size, palette, proportions); only the moving parts change; nothing jitters or drifts
- economy: Capcom-style economical change between frames (small, deliberate pixel changes; cheap NES tricks are good)
- pixel_craft: clean Capcom outlines and clusters in every frame, no noise, orphans or smearing
- timing: the rhythm (how long each frame holds) suits the motion and the enemy's behaviour, the way Capcom times NES enemies
- appeal: the motion adds character and charm in the Capcom manner

Return ONLY a JSON object:
{"subscores": {"motion_readability": n, "consistency": n, "economy": n, "pixel_craft": n, "timing": n, "appeal": n},
 "score": 0-100 overall,
 "verdict": "convincing" or "not_convincing",
 "issues": ["specific, located problems (name the frame)"],
 "fixes": ["specific pixel-level fixes (name the frame)"]}

message.content: {"subscores":{"motion_readability":7,"consistency":8,"economy":6,"pixel_craft":7,"timing":8,"appeal":7},"score":71,"verdict":"not_convincing","issues":["Frame 2 communicates a flare, but its many small curls and alternating black/blue/white clusters make the stroke silhouette busy rather than forceful.","Frame 2 changes large portions of both lower sides as well as every tentacle, making the transition less economical than a typical Capcom two-frame enemy cycle.","Frame 2's screen-right curled limb rises into the body edge and reads partly as a shifting body contour rather than a clearly hinged tentacle.","Frame 2's lower central tentacles create narrow single-pixel notches and crowded high-contrast gaps that look fussier than frame 1's clean clusters.","The 28/10 hold gives a suitable long-glide/short-stroke rhythm, but the instantaneous full flare lacks a strong directional thrust cue."],"fixes":["In frame 2, simplify each outer curl into one clean hooked silhouette, removing the smallest interior black/white notches.","Keep frame 2's torso-side outline identical to frame 1 down to the tentacle roots; begin the flare one or two pixels lower so only the limbs appear to move.","In frame 2, spread the main tentacles outward with fewer bends and align their tips into a clearer backward push shape.","Preserve more of frame 1's central tentacle pixels in frame 2 and change primarily the outer halves, reducing the difference footprint.","In frame 2, consolidate the lower blue and white areas into larger clusters and eliminate isolated one-pixel accents between the central limbs."]}
